title: The lord and the servant (ch. 51)
hookLine: a servant falls into a ditch rushing to serve, and the lord looks on him with love
tomorrow: if prayer doesn't get you what you asked for, what's it for?

cards: You sprint to catch a door for someone with full arms, and you trip on the curb. Now you're the one on the ground, and the person you meant to help is staring down at you.
Julian of Norwich was shown a story much like that: a servant who runs to do his lord's will, and falls into a ditch on the way.

teach.b: In chapter fifty-one, a lord sits in rest and peace, and a servant stands ready. The lord sends him, and the servant doesn't walk. He runs, in haste, for love, to do his lord's will.
And he falls into a slade, a hollow in the ground, and is badly hurt. Julian notices the worst of it.

teach.h: HE CAN'T SEE HIS LORD'S FACE.
teach.b: He groans, and he can't turn his face to see his lord, who is right there. He feels alone. And the lord?
He looks on the servant with pity and love, not blame, because the fall came from his good will. Julian says she took years to understand what she'd been shown.
In the servant she came to see Adam, which means all of us, and also Christ, who comes down into our ditch.
Look how the week gathers here: a fall met without fuss, love as the meaning, a mother who holds, and all shall be well, in one picture.

how: Catholics reading Julian often linger on this chapter as a picture of how God sees human failure; it is read alongside the Church's teaching on the Fall and on Christ's coming.

games.q: what does “the lord and the servant” mean?
o: a parable about a lord who fires a lazy servant
Julian's story of a servant who falls while serving
a feudal law about what servants owe their lords

games.q: the lord and the servant — tap the pairs.
p: he can't turn to see his lord

s: the servant falls because he was careless or lazy
he falls because he ran in haste, for love, to do his lord's will.
the servant's worst pain is that he can't turn to see his lord
the lord is right there; the servant just can't see him.
Julian sees the servant only as Adam
she sees Adam, meaning all of us, and also Christ, who comes down into our ditch.

games.q: a teammate dives to block a shot, collides with the post, and the rebound goes in. she's on the grass, crushed. what does Julian's lord do?
o: remind her she should have stayed on her feet.
see the dive first: she went down trying to serve the team.
say nothing to her until after the game is over.
games.why: the lord looks on the fallen servant with pity and love, because the fall came from good will. the dive comes before the goal.

practice: Count on your fingers three falls from this past month, small ones. For each, name what you were rushing toward when you fell: helping, finishing, pleasing someone.
Then rest, and let the lord's look in Julian's story, the one with no blame in it, rest on all three.

wordCard.voice: The lord and the servant. Julian's story of a servant hurt while rushing to serve, and a lord who looks on him with love.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: he fell rushing to serve, and the look he got had no blame in it. That's the week.

sources.work: Revelations of Divine Love (Julian of Norwich)
